fieldMarks: 11.8-13 in; mostly gray below with an orange face and throat.
Chestnut patch on the belly, reduced on the female.
In flight the short tail shows rusty outer feathers.
Flushes with a rapid cackle; call a hoarse 'kee-ah'.
behavior: Lives in coveys most of the year, in pairs in spring; often unseen while foraging in tall grass.
Feeds on the ground on weed and grass seeds and waste grain (wheat, oats, corn, sunflower); may burrow into snow for seeds in winter; eats insects in summer.
habitat: Cultivated land, hedgerows, bushy pastures and meadows; farmland suits it where hedgerows and shelterbelts remain between fields.
In winter often in stubble fields, moving into woodlot edges in harsh weather.
range: Introduced from Europe (as early as the 1790s, established later); most successful on the northern prairies and present in eastern Canada, the Great Lakes, the Northwest and the Rocky Mountain region.
